title: Move Like Harlem
sub: Grades 5–8 · Physical Education · The Lindy Hop, the Charleston and the Savoy Ballroom
objective: Students will explore the physical vocabulary of Harlem Renaissance dance — the Lindy Hop, Charleston, and jazz movement — understanding these not as performance spectacle but as a form of cultural expression, community building, and joyful resistance. They will connect rhythmic movement to musical structure, develop coordination through partner and group patterns, and reflect on dance as embodied history.
materials: **Audio:** upbeat jazz — recommended: Chick Webb, “Stompin’ at the Savoy” (1934); Duke Ellington, “It Don’t Mean a Thing” (1932). Both free on YouTube.
Open gym space or cleared classroom; no equipment needed
Optional: short video clip of Lindy Hop dancers at the Savoy Ballroom (several authentic clips on YouTube)
Differentiated reflection handouts — one per student (completed after activity)
connection: **Option 1 — Visit the exhibition:** bring your class to experience the phonograph, the Great Migration Map, the Jazz Lab, and more. Ask your librarian to arrange a visit.
**Option 2 — Virtual visit:** online at the address below.

steps.title: The Savoy Ballroom
script: *“The Savoy Ballroom opened in Harlem in 1926. It held 4,000 people. Black and white dancers danced together — which was illegal in many other places in America. The Lindy Hop was born there. It was named after Charles Lindbergh’s transatlantic flight in 1927 — people said the dancers looked like they were flying. Today we’re going to move the way Harlem moved.”*

steps.title: Jazz walk and rhythm
script: Students walk to the beat of jazz music. Teacher calls out: **freeze** (hold pose), **slow motion** (half speed), **double time** (double speed), **mirror** (copy teacher’s arm movements while walking). Purpose: establishes rhythmic listening and body awareness before structured movement.

steps.title: Charleston Step
script: Teach the basic Charleston: step forward on right, kick left foot forward; step back on left, kick right foot back. Count 1-2-3-4. Once secure: add arm swing. Once secure: try with partner in mirror.

steps.title: Lindy Hop Basics
script: Introduce the rock-step: rock back on left (count 1), replace weight onto right (count 2); then triple step left-right-left (counts 3-and-4) and triple step right-left-right (counts 5-and-6). This is the 6-count basic, the first step most Lindy Hop classes teach. Practice solo, then in loose pairs (not holding hands — just facing).

steps.title: Creative Response
script: Students in groups of 3–4. Give each group a card: **Joy / Protest / Journey / Arrival in Harlem**. Groups create a 16-count movement sequence using the vocabulary they’ve learned that expresses their word. Share with one other group.

steps.title: Cool-down and reflection
script: Slow walk to music cooling down. Ask: *“Where in your body did you feel the rhythm most? What did it feel like to move to music that was made about 100 years ago?”* Students complete reflection handout.
